repos.name: thedotmack/claude-mem
repos.description: Persistent Context Across Sessions for Every Agent – Captures everything your agent does during sessions, compresses it with AI, and injects relevant context back into future sessions. Works with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, Copilot, OpenCode + More
repos.eli5: It’s like a notebook that automatically writes down everything a smart helper does, shrinks the notes so they fit in a pocket, and then shows the important parts the next time you talk to the helper. Programmers who build AI assistants use it.

repos.name: lightpanda-io/browser
repos.description: Lightpanda: the headless browser designed for AI and automation
repos.eli5: Imagine a tiny, super‑fast robot that can open web pages and read them without needing a big, heavy browser; it’s built for other robots to use. Developers who need quick web data for AI or automation use it.

repos.name: shiyu-coder/Kronos
repos.description: Kronos: A Foundation Model for the Language of Financial Markets
repos.eli5: It’s like a translator that reads stock charts as a language and helps computers understand market moves, trained on lots of real data. Financial analysts and AI researchers use it.

repos.name: pingdotgg/t3code
repos.eli5: Think of a remote control that lets you steer many AI helpers on your computer from your phone or web page, like a game controller for coding bots. Developers who work with AI agents use it.

repos.name: milind-soni/OpenMausBot
repos.description: Open-source Grok Bot alternative with a virtual machine that bots can use
repos.eli5: It’s a playground where you can chat with different AI bots that each have their own personality, all running on your own computer like having a team of helpers. Anyone who wants a private AI chat team uses it.

repos.name: public-apis/public-apis
repos.description: A collective list of free APIs
repos.eli5: It’s a big library catalog that lists free web services you can call, like a phone book for internet tools. Programmers looking for ready‑made data sources use it.

repos.name: cjpais/Handy
repos.description: A free, open source, and extensible speech-to-text application that works completely offline.
repos.eli5: It’s a voice‑to‑text recorder that works on your computer without sending anything to the internet, like a personal dictation notebook. Anyone who wants to type by speaking offline uses it.

repos.name: Donchitos/Claude-Code-Game-Studios
repos.description: Turn Claude Code into a full game dev studio — 49 AI agents, 72 workflow skills, and a complete coordination system mirroring real studio hierarchy.
repos.eli5: It turns one AI helper into a whole game‑making studio, giving each helper a job like a director or artist, so building a game feels like working with a real team. Game developers using AI use it.

repos.name: kornia/kornia
repos.description: 🐍 Geometric Computer Vision Library for Spatial AI
repos.eli5: It’s a toolbox that lets computers edit and understand pictures the same way you can draw or move things on paper, but it works inside AI programs. Researchers and developers in computer vision use it.

repos.name: beenuar/AiSOC
repos.description: Open-source AI Security Operations Center: alert fusion, LLM-agent triage, MITRE ATT&CK investigation, and a replayable decision ledger for every agent step. Self-hostable, runs with no API keys, MIT licensed. Ships an MCP server for Claude, Cursor and Continue.
repos.eli5: It’s like a security guard that watches all the alarms on a computer, asks a smart robot to investigate, and keeps a notebook of every step so you can see what happened. Security teams use it to protect systems.
